LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for x86_64 and aarch64 architectures that point to prebuilt tar.gz binaries hosted in the official GitHub repository under a versioned release URL. The `source` arrays use standard syntax and fetch from a predictable, static tag-based release URL constructed from `pkgver`. There are no command substitutions, `git` operations, or remote code executions in the global scope or within `pkgver()` — in fact, no `pkgver()` function is defined, so the version remains static.

Checksums are provided for both architectures via `sha256sums_x86_64` and `sha256sums_aarch64`, meaning the downloaded binaries will be verified against known hashes. Even if the checksums were 'SKIP', that would not make this phase unsafe, but in this case, they are present and valid. The top-level scope contains only safe variable assignments and URL construction without side effects. No network requests or file operations beyond the intended source download occur during sourcing.

Since `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will only source the PKGBUILD, resolve the source URLs, and download the tarballs (without extracting or running anything), and because no malicious code execution occurs during sourcing, this operation is safe.
</details>
<summary>
No dangerous code in sourcing or download phase
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub repository (esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix) matching the declared upstream URL. The sources are versioned release assets over HTTPS, and architecture-specific SHA-256 checksums are provided, ensuring integrity verification during package building. No network operations, dynamic downloads, or execution of fetched content occur at build or install time beyond the standard extraction of the source tarballs.

The `package()` function safely installs the binary by searching for it in predictable locations within the extracted source directory, using standard `install` commands with appropriate permissions. It does not employ dangerous constructs like `eval`, obfuscated code, or unexpected system modifications. The use of `find` is limited to locating the binary locally and is not combined with any malicious payloads.

While the package skips stripping debug symbols via `options=('!strip')`, this is a common practice for some binaries and not inherently unsafe. There are no post-install hooks, systemd services, or file operations outside the package directory. All actions are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for distributing a precompiled binary.
</details>
<summary>
Standard binary package with verified upstream sources
</summary>
